title: lebre: online forecasting with statistically tested structural changes
description:
Installable Python library implementing LEBRE v0.54, an online one-step-ahead forecaster for a target driven by exogenous inputs, at a counted cost per step (median 870 floating-point operations per step in the final evaluation). It has three layers: a structural core whose structural changes, removals included, are accepted only when an anytime-valid e-process of predictive improvement crosses a level set by an online multiple-testing rule; M1, a precision expert combined with the core by AdaHedge, which sleeps while it carries no weight and wakes by evidence; and M2, which starts the output from a declared trivial reference and combines two paths by an (A,B)-Prod. With the three v0.54 changes switched off it is LEBRE v0.53 (lebre 0.2.0); the core alone (lebre 0.1.0) remains available.

LEBRE v0.54 was promoted by a pre-registered rule in the research record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23376152; https://github.com/Iquitim/lebre-research): on 93 reserved series it kept the error of v0.53 (ratio 0.989 to 1.000 per family, no harm in any family) at a median per-series cost of 0.905 of v0.53's (95% CI 0.857-0.932). In the reference environment (Windows, CPython 3.11, NumPy 2.2.5) its forecasts are bit-for-bit identical to the promoted research code.

Scope and limits. One-step forecasting; the cost cut is about 10% at the median and none where M1 helps; a relation that disappears for more than about 5,200 steps and returns is removed and must be re-detected; spurious inputs in level series can still be accepted and the cycle must be declared; no formal guarantee in the original scale for M1 and M2; no component is original. See the research record for the full evidence and its limits.
